recipes.name: Mouse's Macaroni and Cheese
ingredients_raw: 8 ounces processed cheese food (eg. Velveeta), cubed

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (205 degrees C). Butter a 1 1/2 quart casserole dish. Bring a saucepan of lightly salted water to a boil. Add macaroni, and cook until not quite done, about 6 minutes. Drain.

In a separate saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Blend in the flour, mustard powder, and pepper until smooth. Slowly stir in the milk, beating out any lumps. Add the American and processed cheeses, and stir constantly until the sauce is thick and smooth.
Drain noodles, and stir them into the cheese sauce. Transfer the mixture to the prepared casserole dish. Sprinkle bread crumbs over the top.
Cover the dish, and bake for 20 to 25 minutes, or until sauce is thick and bubbly.

raw_recipe.headline: Mouse's Macaroni and Cheese
raw_recipe.description: A dash of mustard powder and grind of black pepper adds extra kick to a creamy cheese sauce. Stir cooked macaroni into the sauce and bake with a layer of bread crumbs over the top.

review.reviewBody:
This recipe is to die for. However, I gave it 4 stars because I had to adjust it a bit to make it work. The other reviewers are right, the cheese to noodle ratio is way off. The mouse likes her cheese a little too much! The macaroni has to be doubled to 3 cups, and I found it does best in a roomy 2 or 2.5 quart casserole dish.

Since I'm not a huge fan of so much velveeta and processed cheeses, I went out in search of the perfect blend and found Kraft's "Classic Melts" shredded cheese blend. It's a combo of American cheese, sharp cheddar, white cheddar, and monterey jack. I got two of the 8 oz. bags.

I am pregnant, and this is my all-time #1 craving. Better than the Cracker Barrel's Mac & Cheese. :)

This is a fantastic recipe. I have modified it for my taste - but use the recipe as a starting point for your own tastes. 1st, the amount of macaroni may seem small - but it’s correct because the Mac will absorb sauce/expand in the oven. My modifications: I use 1/2 lb of Land o Lakes American cheese and 1/2 lb of either Monterey Jack OR pepper jack cheese. Land o lakes is worth it cause it’s far more like cheese and much less like plastic. I cut everything up into cubes and alternate adding to the roux/milk base to make sure everything is melted smoothly. I’m also constantly whisking the sauce as I add the cheeses. I’ve only received rave reviews when serving this and it is a family favorite.

I have been making this macaroni and cheese on a regular basis for about a year now and it's delicious the way it is. I'm only adding my changes here because this is how my family likes it and I needed somewhere to put my notes lol!

I used 16oz uncooked elbow macaroni. Increase the bechamel sauce by 1.5, add just a touch of salt, and brown the butter/flour mixture slightly before adding milk. add the Velveeta to the bechamel and let cook on very low heat for about 7 or 8 mins (or while macaroni boils). Remove sauce from heat and let the mix cool just a little before adding the 8oz room temperature grated sharp cheddar. This method results in ridiculously smooth cheese sauce. Not at all gritty. I had to physically stop myself from eating the hot cheese sauce straight out of the saucepan.

I also didn't even bother with the bread crumbs or baking it, just cooked the noodles enough to make it ready to eat.

I agree that a 2 qt dish is required, but I disagree about the pasta to cheese ratio. Maybe Mouse and I are kindred cheese spirits? I absolutely loved it, but I had to make several of my own tweaks to get it perfect.

I left out the mustard powder because I didn't have any, but it didn't taste like it's lacking (although I don't know what it tastes like with it, so...) I sautéed diced onion and garlic in the butter before adding the flour and pepper. I also don't like processed cheese taste, so I just used regular cheddar, but I imagine you could sub any cheese and it would be delish! I didn't have 18 oz of cheese, only 13 so that's how much I used and it was plenty cheesy! I always use Panko instead of regular breadcrumbs, which I highly recommend. Much better crisp! I don't like "runny" mac and cheese, so I cooked it UNCOVERED to make sure enough liquid evaporated. It did require the full 25 minutes to thicken up for me, and then I broiled it for about 5 minutes to get a little crunch on the top. I also let it set for 15 minutes after coming out of the oven. I will certainly make this again, and again, and again!

I modified it to make it the BEST mac n cheese I've ever had in my life. Hands down. Those of you who don't like modified reviews, please move on. I sauteed 1/2 small onion in butter and added adobe seasoning to that. I crumbled 1 lb hamburg in a separate pan and sprinkled a little bit of worcestershire sauce in the hamburg (this added so much flavor). I added a 1/2 tsp. of better than bullion (chicken flavor) to the milk/onion/flour mixture (before I added the cheese), and a tiny dab of brown mustard, this creates so much depth of flavor. I then mixed the hamburg in with the cooked macaroni, mixed the cheese sauce in with that and baked it with the bread crumbs on top. Literally to die for. I used half velveeta and half shredded cheese mixture. It doesn't get better than this.

Very good. I made changes to suit my families taste. I only use about 2oz of Velveeta and 8oz of sharp cheddar cheese, grated. I add about 1 tsp of Franks Hot Sauce, too. I also use about 3 cups milk ..we like it nice and saucy. For the topping, I grate 2 slices of French bread in the food processor and mix with 2 Tbsp of melted butter and spinkle on top. I bake it, uncovered, at 350 in an 8"square pan.

This was a very creamy and cheesy mac n cheese. I will definitely use this recipe from now on, but for me the pasta to sauce ratio was way off. I followed the reviews advising not to add pasta, but I ended up with more a cheese soup with pasta. Next time I'll add 1/4 to 1/2 cup more pasta OR 1/2 cup to 1 cup more pasta for a double recipe which is what I made. Also, I cooked pasta for one minute less than the package directions (8 min) and still felt it was more chewy than I'd like after coming out of the oven. So next time I'll just follow package directions and cook all the way. I used off brand velveeta and fiesta blend shredded cheese from Wal-Mart. I reduced pepper to 1/2 ts and added 1 ts of onion powder and paprika and 1/2 ts of salt. I also added some chicken thigh to make this more of a complete meal and that was a great addition (2 chicken thighs for a double recipe).

Excellent classic recipe! I twisted it a little to make it taste just like my mom's by: first, doubling the recipe and then decreasing the cheese by 25% and increasing the milk by 1/2 cup. I also added a cup of finely chopped sauteed onions and skipped the mustard powder. It's perfect; thanks for the help Mouse!

Don’t change the proportions until you try it once. Once you bake it, the ratio is great. It sets up. Here are the changes I made: didn’t have American cheese so I used shredded sharp cheddar with the velveeta. I only had Panko, which turned out to be awesome. I baked it covered as directed, but I wanted to brown the Panko so i took the cover off after 20 minutes. I think it was about 10 minutes more before they browned. My husband and I kept saying this is so good!” after almost every bite.

Will make it again! Easy recipe with delicious results! Topped with 1/3 breadcrumbs 1/3 French fried onions and 1/3 crushed wavy potato chips to try different flavors and textures! Added diced onion to butter as it melted.. nice addition!
This mac & cheese was GREAT! I used crushed potato chips on top instead of bread crumbs. Very tasty!
This was amazing! So much flavor!
This is everyone's favorite I've even heard kids ask their mom why couldn't they make it like mine
This is my favorite, go-to mac & cheese recipe!
The family loved it. Creamy , cheesie comfort food.
It's perfect as is. However, on a hunch once, I added 8oz of Smoked Gouda and then did 4oz each of American and Velveeta. It's requested at every pot luck I attend. Try it, you'll thank me later.

Like other reviewers, I switched out the American cheese for 8 ounces of cheddar. I also used white pepper instead of black pepper so my kids would eat it. The ratios are correct and it makes a delicious final product when baked.
I've been using this recipe about 15 years. People still ask for it at family get togethers.
